producer.candidate: numpy.linalg.solve; wrong-answer explicitly altered; zero-preconditioner explicitly altered
producer.scope: Original mathematical equations, not hardware or measured data
producer.oracle: Exact analytic ladder Green function; independent rational Gauss-Jordan for smaller systems

examples.title: FiPy · final transient
examples.description: 400 cells, 1,920 coefficients. Check the original final-step corner decision without a dense inverse.

examples.title: FiPy · steady state
examples.description: The same NIST application after its steady-state solve. Positive weights enable a sparse proof.

examples.title: When weights fail
examples.description: The steady-state equations with unit weights. A failed premise does not mean a singular system.

examples.title: A changed answer
examples.description: The steady-state candidate with corner 19 set to zero. The valid bound must lose the threshold claim.

examples.title: A voltage decision with evidence
examples.description: An original ideal 64-node resistor ladder. Certify whether node 32 is above 16 V; this models equations, not measured hardware.

examples.title: Small residual, bounded error
examples.description: Original ill-conditioned stored binary64 equations. A small floating residual alone does not establish answer accuracy.

examples.title: Small residual, failed proof
examples.description: Original ill-conditioned stored binary64 equations. A small floating residual alone does not establish answer accuracy.

examples.title: An unsupported decision
examples.description: A deliberately altered answer has a tiny residual. Its wide valid enclosure cannot establish the threshold claim.

examples.title: A refused certificate
examples.description: Even a correct answer cannot pass this proof with an unusable zero approximate inverse. Refusal is useful information.
